source.title: Maximum Number of Events That Can Be Attended

teaching.hint: When several events are available today, which one loses its chance to be attended first?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Choosing the currently available event with the earliest ending day preserves maximum flexibility for later days.
solution_outline.approach: Process days in order, adding newly opened events and discarding expired ones. Attend the available event with the earliest deadline; skip stretches with no open event.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The available set contains exactly the unopened-by-choice events whose start has passed and end has not passed; the selected count is feasible.
solution_outline.correctness: An exchange moves an earliest-deadline event into today's slot without reducing an optimal schedule: a later-deadline event can use any later slot occupied by the former. Repeating aligns an optimum with each choice.
solution_outline.complexity: O(m log m) time and O(m) auxiliary space for m events; each event enters and leaves the ordered candidate set once.
solution_outline.pitfall: Attending an event that ends later can make an earlier-deadline event expire.

common_wrong_turns: Sort only by start day and take the first available event
source_fidelity_notes: The diagram and long schedule transcript were removed; inclusive attendance days and one-event-per-day semantics remain.
